questions.question: Give an example for Anti Markownikoff addition.
questions.solution_html:
• Give an example for Anti-Markownikoff addition.
  • A classic example is the hydroboration-oxidation of propene or the addition of HBr
  • to propene in the presence of peroxides (Kharasch effect), which yields 1-
  • bromopropane.

questions.question: Identify the electrophile involved in the sulphonation of benzene.
questions.solution_html:
• Identify the electrophile involved in the sulphonation of benzene.
  • The active electrophile in the sulphonation of benzene is sulfur trioxide (SO3). Even
  • though it is neutral, the sulfur atom is highly electron-deficient.

questions.question: Identify the specific reactive intermediate formed during the electrophilic addition of HBr to ethene.
questions.solution_html:
• Identify the specific reactive intermediate formed during the electrophilic addition of
  • HBr to ethene.
  • The reactive intermediate formed is a carbocation, specifically the ethyl carbocation
  • (CH3CH2+).

questions.question: Define the term Enantiomer.
questions.solution_html:
• Define the term Enantiomer.
  • Enantiomers are a pair of stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of
  • each other. They have identical physical properties except for the direction in which
  • they rotate plane-polarized light.

questions.question: State Auwers-Skita rule.
questions.solution_html:
• State Auwers-Skita rule.
  • The Auwers-Skita rule states that among alicyclic diastereomers, the isomer with the
  • higher boiling point, higher refractive index, and higher density is generally the cis-
  • isomer.

questions.question: Draw the most stable and unstable conformation of cyclohexane.
questions.solution_html:
• Draw the most stable and unstable conformation of cyclohexane.
  • The chair conformation is the most stable due to minimized torsional and steric strain.
  • The half-chair is considered the most unstable, though the boat conformation is also a
  • high-energy, unstable form.

questions.question: Identify the configuration if the two groups of lowest priority are on the same side of the double bond.
questions.solution_html:
• Identify the configuration if the two groups of lowest priority are on the same side of
  • the double bond.
  • In the E/Z system, if the two higher-priority groups are on the same side, it is the Z-
  • configuration (zusammen); if the question implies the "lowest" priority groups are on
  • the same side (meaning high priority are also on the same side), it is Z.

questions.question: List two examples of synthetic rubber.
questions.solution_html:
• List two examples of synthetic rubber.
  • Two common examples are Neoprene (polychloroprene) and Buna-S (Styrene-
  • Butadiene Rubber).

questions.question: Illustrate the simple repeating pattern of a block copolymer using A and B notations.
questions.solution_html:
• Illustrate the simple repeating pattern of a block copolymer using A and B notations.
  • A block copolymer consists of long sequences of one monomer followed by long
  • sequences of another, represented as: -A-A-A-A-B-B-B-B-.

questions.question: Recall the repeating unit of Polyethylene. [2x10 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Recall the repeating unit of Polyethylene.
  • The repeating unit of polyethylene is -(CH2-CH2)-.

questions.question: Write a note on elctrophiles.
questions.solution_html:
• Write a note on electrophiles.
  • Electrophiles are electron-loving species that are either positively charged (H+, NO2+)
  • or neutral molecules with vacant orbitals (BF3, AlCl3). They attack regions of high
  • electron density during a chemical reaction.

questions.question: Write a note on homolytic and heterolytic fission.
questions.solution_html:
• Write a note on homolytic and heterolytic fission.
  • • Homolytic Fission: A covalent bond breaks such that each atom retains one electron
  • from the shared pair, resulting in the formation of free radicals.
  • • Heterolytic Fission: The bond breaks such that both electrons are retained by one of
  • the atoms (usually the more electronegative one), resulting in the formation of ions
  • (cations and anions).

questions.question: Compare E1 and E2 reactions.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare E1 and E2 reactions.
  • • E1 (Unimolecular Elimination): Occurs in two steps via a carbocation intermediate;
  • the rate depends only on the substrate concentration.
  • • E2 (Bimolecular Elimination): Occurs in a single concerted step where the base
  • abstracts a proton at the same time the leaving group departs; the rate depends on both
  • the substrate and the base.

questions.question: Compare polar and non-polar molecules.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare polar and non-polar molecules.
  • • Polar Molecules: Have an uneven distribution of electron density due to differences in
  • electronegativity between atoms, resulting in a permanent dipole moment (e.g., H2O).
  • • Non-polar Molecules: Electrons are shared equally (e.g., Cl2) or the molecular
  • geometry causes bond dipoles to cancel out (e.g., CO2), resulting in a zero net dipole
  • moment.

questions.question: Explain why a Meso compound is optically inactive.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain why a Meso compound is optically inactive.
  • A meso compound contains chiral centers but is optically inactive because it possesses an
  • internal plane of symmetry. The optical rotation caused by one half of the molecule is
  • exactly cancelled by the equal and opposite rotation of the other half (internal
  • compensation).

questions.question: Identify and Explain the two types of optical rotation- dextrorotatory and laevorotatory.
questions.solution_html:
• Identify and explain the two types of optical rotation.
  • • Dextrorotatory (d or +): A compound that rotates the plane of polarized light to the
  • right (clockwise).
  • • Laevorotatory (l or -): A compound that rotates the plane of polarized light to the left
  • (counter-clockwise).

questions.question: Describe the step-by-step preparation of Nylon 6,6.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the step-by-step preparation of Nylon 6,6. Nylon 6,6 is prepared by the
  • condensation polymerization of adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine.

questions.question: Classify polymers based on intermolecular forces with suitable examples for each category. [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Classify polymers based on intermolecular forces.
  • • Elastomers: Very weak forces (e.g., Buna-S).
  • • Fibers: Strong intermolecular forces like hydrogen bonding (e.g., Nylon 6,6).
  • • Thermoplastics: Intermediate forces; can be softened by heating (e.g., Polyethylene).
  • • Thermosetting Polymers: Heavily cross-linked; cannot be remolded (e.g., Bakelite).

questions.question: Write an essay on Inductive effect.
questions.solution_html:
• Write an essay on Inductive effect.
  • The inductive effect is the permanent displacement of sigma (sigma) electrons along a
  • chain of carbon atoms due to the presence of an atom or group of different
  • electronegativity.
  • • -I Effect (Electron-withdrawing): Groups like -NO2, -Cl, and -COOH pull electrons
  • away from the carbon chain.
  • • +I Effect (Electron-releasing): Groups like alkyl groups (-CH3) push electrons toward
  • the carbon chain. It is a distance-dependent effect that weakens as it moves further
  • from the substituent.

questions.question: Write an essay on SN¹ reactions and SN² reactions.
questions.solution_html:
• Write an essay on SN1 and SN2 reactions.
  • • SN1 (Unimolecular Nucleophilic Substitution): A two-step mechanism involving a
  • carbocation intermediate. It is favoured by tertiary halides and polar protic solvents.
  • The reaction often results in racemization.
  • • SN2 (Bimolecular Nucleophilic Substitution): A one-step concerted mechanism
  • involving a transition state. The nucleophile attacks from the backside, leading to
  • complete inversion of configuration (Walden Inversion). It is favoured by primary
  • halides.

questions.question: Describe in detail the conformational analysis of n-butane.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe in detail the conformational analysis of n-butane. Rotation around the C2-C3
  • bond of n-butane results in several conformations:
  • • Fully Eclipsed: Highest energy due to maximum steric and torsional strain.
  • • Gauche: Staggered but with methyl groups close to each other (intermediate stability).
  • • Eclipsed: High energy.
  • • Anti (Staggered): Lowest energy and most stable because the bulky methyl groups are
  • 180 degrees apart.

questions.question: Compare and Contrast addition and condensation polymerization. [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Compare and contrast addition and condensation polymerization.
  • • Addition Polymerization: Monomers (usually containing double bonds) join together
  • without the loss of any small molecules. The polymer has the same empirical formula
  • as the monomer (e.g., Polyvinyl Chloride).
  • • Condensation Polymerization: Monomers (containing bifunctional groups) react with
  • the elimination of small molecules like H2O, NH3, or HCl. The process is step-wise
  • (e.g., Polyesters, Terylene).
